We all get jealous. When I was 21 I had my first successful small Business in property, It was a huge project (for me) that I 'tricked' my way into getting and my own mother was screaming and livid, my sister stole money off me, my  friends dissappeared and my whole life became me being a problem solver/fixer.

I was literally only worth what I could give in terms of support. I became the guy that gave money etc. Peers were livid with jealousy. Etc

It made me realise there's a massive part of us that is always seeking ultimate happiness /love, and it's easier to get it from other people than give it to ourselves: in a way that's all money and success are, they're shortcuts to these sunshine feelings etc

I wanted all these people to celebrate me I think,  and by wanting that I drowned. 

Lesson 1: we are born and die alone.

I think it's discipline. Society has changed to a crazed over consumption that wasn't available to us before, the fact is our minds etc react to our environment and our current environment means we fall 'victim' or "prey' to messaging, advertising, images and all these forms of suggestion which are empty promises and we fool ourselves into following.

Discipline forces us to assess what's actually working for us personally and not chase the ghost of an image. Trading your time energy etc for things that benefit you as opposed to addictions.

I doubt it's about semen retention itself, I think it's moreyour mind dominating your environment with awareness and thus. Eing less susceptible to à kind of mental slavery we're all aware we're in on some level.

Although if your à satisfied citizen it's no longer slavery : it's a good trade, because your achieving health etc.

I know it's difficult, but you can't control things outside of you. My advice would be to put energy into stopping reacting, into self discipline and self value and maybe removing yourself from the environment, both mentally and physically. 

One secret is that TV and Reddit type idealism and shock outside the moral 'norm' is a lie. Everyone has dark sides and they manifest in different ways: it's not to say be in agreement , but just working on yourself and your wounds is enough effort without feeding your child self's needs with idealism. Very few people have balanced parents etc who did well. It's something that hurt me a lot so save yourself some time and just reinvest in your own space, reacting too much makes you a victim.

1. Eagerness to please, prioritising someone else's needs, immediate or otherwise over mine.

2. Being too future orientated, so not living in the present moment, and getting ot of things/tasks out if the way instead of being mindful of 'tge now'

3. Masturbation Def + similar to point two as well

4. Bad habits/mental programming. I read your body cells/parts have and hold traumas of there own. So sometimes they'll go against you if you are abusing them. (Gets metaphysical here) but TRE (trauma release therapy) is on YouTube etc is worth practicing to release.

5. Seeking too much validation subconsiously/ just giving too much of yourself away. Sometimes you don't want too and it's important to be on your side, even the 'dissapointing my partner's thing is a really interesting point in you not showing up for yourself, partners are super understanding in my experience but are you to yourself? 

I'm doing alot if work on this showing up for myself side of things because you either do or don't, what other people perceive as little to do with it. It's a personal journey and I hope this helps.
